title: Console rollouts: wizard backend contracts (preview/validate/submit) + response models
author: Chloe Martin
description:
Summary

This PR updates the Console backend contract endpoints used by the Hosted canary rollout wizard. It introduces a stable 3-call flow (preview -> validate -> submit) with explicit response models for: computed schedule normalization, policy guardrail feedback, warnings, and human-readable validation errors that can be shown directly in the wizard review screen.

Motivation

The wizard needs to (a) show the user exactly what will happen before creating a rollout, (b) run the same policy/validation checks used at submission time, and (c) return structured, actionable errors (including approval-gate requirements) so users don’t discover issues only after a failed submit. Existing endpoints were partially shared with the legacy rollout editor and returned internal models that were hard to safely render and difficult to keep backwards compatible.

What changed

New/updated endpoints (Console backend -> Orchestrator)

- POST /console/v1/hosted/routes/{route_id}/rollouts/preview
  - Input: baseline + canary target (model version/config), optional traffic schedule draft, guardrail overrides (if allowed), and stop-conditions selection
  - Output: normalized plan (step percentages + computed soak windows), derived cohorting key, computed rollout “diff” summary, and warnings

- POST /console/v1/hosted/routes/{route_id}/rollouts/validate
  - Runs policy evaluation + semantic validations (schedule monotonicity, max step jump, min soak, approval gates, stop-condition constraints)
  - Output: ok=true/false, blocking_errors[], non_blocking_warnings[], required_approvals (if any), and an “allowed_actions” set used by the UI to enable/disable the submit button

- POST /console/v1/hosted/routes/{route_id}/rollouts/submit
  - Idempotent submit (client provides request_id)
  - Creates the rollout via orchestrator and returns rollout_id + the same normalized plan returned by preview to keep the wizard state consistent

Response model updates

- Introduces RolloutWizardPlanV1 (explicit versioned DTO) rather than returning internal orchestrator models.
- Adds explicit error taxonomy:
  - POLICY_DENIED (includes policy_rule_id, user_facing_message)
  - VALIDATION_ERROR (field + message)
  - APPROVAL_REQUIRED (includes required_role)
  - CONFLICT (e.g., another active rollout exists on the route)
- Adds warnings with stable codes used for UI copy (e.g., WARN_SOAK_TOO_SHORT, WARN_LARGE_STEP_JUMP_REQUESTED_BUT_CAPPED).
- Includes an optional “policy_context” block (tier, entitlements, default guardrails) in preview/validate responses so the UI can render “why can’t I do this?” explanations without additional calls.

Backwards compatibility

- Keeps legacy console rollout endpoints intact (used by existing rollout list/details pages).
- New wizard endpoints are gated behind the hosted_canary_rollout_wizard flag and are only used by the new wizard flow.
- DTOs are versioned (PlanV1, ValidationV1). Any incompatible changes will require PlanV2 rather than silently reshaping fields.

Security / auth

- Enforces route-scoped permission checks for preview/validate/submit.
- submit additionally checks “rollout.create” and returns POLICY_DENIED with a user-facing message when the user lacks permission.
- validate returns “required_approvals” but does not leak approver identities; UI only shows the role needed (e.g., rollout-approver).

Notes for reviewers

- The validate endpoint intentionally duplicates some checks done by submit. This is to ensure UI can show deterministic results before the user confirms and to avoid “passed preview, failed submit” surprises. submit still re-runs validation.
- submit is idempotent via request_id to prevent double-creation when users double-click or the network retries.

Testing

- Added unit tests for schedule normalization and warning emission.
- Added contract tests for error mapping from policy engine errors to Console DTOs.
- Manual test: wizard flow in staging (preview -> validate -> submit) using a route with an active fallback policy + region routing.

Release notes

- Adds versioned wizard contracts for Hosted canary rollouts (preview/validate/submit).
- Improved user-facing validation and policy guardrail messaging in the rollout wizard.

Screens / API examples

Example validate response for approval gate:
- ok: false
- blocking_errors: [ { code: APPROVAL_REQUIRED, message: "Approval required to exceed 25% step increase", required_role: "rollout-approver" } ]

Related

- ENG-9140 (orchestrator service endpoints)
- ENG-9146 (policy engine guardrails)
- DES-742 (wizard UI)

Checklist

- [x] Versioned DTOs
- [x] Idempotent submit
- [x] Policy error mapping w/ user-facing messages
- [x] Contract tests
- [x] Feature-flagged usage

conversation:
Dylan Brooks: Can we guarantee validate and submit run the same checks? I don't want the wizard to say “OK” and then submit fails because of a different codepath.

Chloe Martin (author): Yep. validate calls the same underlying validator used by submit (submit re-runs it). The only extra in submit is the active-rollout conflict check and create call. Added a regression test for “validate OK then submit OK” with the same input.

Jordan Lee: POLICY_DENIED should include a stable rule identifier so the Console can map to copy without parsing messages.

Chloe Martin (author): Added policy_rule_id to POLICY_DENIED and APPROVAL_REQUIRED responses. Messages remain user-facing but UI can key off rule ids if we decide to later.

Tessa Morgan: Warnings need stable codes for UX copy; free-form strings will drift.

Chloe Martin (author): Agreed. Converted warnings to { code, message, severity } and kept message for now as default copy. UI can override by code.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Please double-check we’re not leaking any tenant-level entitlements beyond what the user can already infer. The “policy_context” block is useful, but keep it minimal.

Chloe Martin (author): Scoped policy_context to only include the effective guardrail defaults + tier name + feature flag state. Removed internal entitlement ids and any org-level metadata.
